yourBench.stressBody: Your unoptimized copies are sent only now and then, so they rarely find your provider's cache warm; without the layer, every request would. Priced as if every input token of each copy had been read from cache — at the cached-input rate of the price table, or free when it has none — the lower bound is {lower}.

yourBench.methodBody: Each pair is one request: what the unoptimized copy cost and what the optimized request cost, both from your provider's usage counters at the price table's rates. A pair counts only when the copy finished normally and met your output contract, the same rule your own requests must pass to be checked. Requests are grouped by how the layer served them, and each group is weighted by its share of your eligible requests. The interval is a stratified percentile bootstrap: {resamples} resamples, seed {seed}. With the CSV and the counts on this page you can recompute every point estimate; your intervals will match ours within resampling noise.

caveats.sample: A random sample, not every request: the figures describe your eligible traffic with the uncertainty shown, and they are never turned into an amount to bill.
caveats.randomness: Two calls rarely answer alike unless you fix the seed and set temperature to zero. That widens the interval. A pair counts only when both sides finished normally, so an answer cut off on one side only is never counted as a saving.
caveats.outside: Costs outside your provider call, such as an embedding service you run yourself, are in neither side.
caveats.streaming: Requests that failed, or that you cancelled while streaming, are not counted.

installLicensePanel.heading: Three steps. Your prompts never touch our servers.
installLicensePanel.step1: 1 · Your keys (optional) — the SDK is open core: with no key it runs in COMMUNITY mode (every local lever on, zero telemetry). A key that is set but invalid still fails closed. Passed as licenseKey.
installLicensePanel.step2: 2 · Create & verify a service-account key — a machine credential (bvk_…) that does two jobs: it reports counts-only usage (your seats & savings), and it lets the SDK and the gateway collect your renewed license by themselves every billing period. Separate from the license key; only its hash is stored. Create one, then Test my key to confirm it's live.
installLicensePanel.shownOnce: shown once at creation — only the prefix is stored.
installLicensePanel.renewalNote: Keep this key in your deployment. Your license expires at the end of each billing period and the renewal mints a new one. With this key the SDK collects it and swaps it in without a restart. Without it nobody collects it, so someone has to paste the new key by hand every period — and if nobody does, the SDK stops once the grace period ends, even though the subscription is paid and up to date.
installLicensePanel.step3: 3 · Set it up with one command — the recommended way. Run it in your project's folder:
installLicensePanel.initNote: It reads your package.json (Next.js, Express, the Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangChain.js, the Anthropic SDK or the OpenAI SDK) and prints what your stack needs: the install line for your package manager, which keys are still missing, the exact code for your adapter and a check that spends no tokens — the layer answers it on your machine, without calling the model. It writes nothing: --write creates new files only, after asking you, and never overwrites an existing one.
installLicensePanel.manualInstall: Prefer to wire it by hand? Install the package — public on npm, no token, no config:
installLicensePanel.manualWire: …then wire your provider and read the SavingsReport:
installLicensePanel.gatewayNote: Coding agent instead of an app? The same package ships a local measuring gateway: bvsala claude launches Claude Code through it and this dashboard shows the spend, token by token. It starts with no keys at all (COMMUNITY mode); the optional service key from step 2 adds this dashboard and org entitlements.
installLicensePanel.doctorComment: other agents and SDKs: the exact configuration for each
installLicensePanel.agentsNote: Each wrapper sets its agent up for that session only — nothing in its configuration changes — and on exit tells you how many requests it metered, which ones it could not, and why. bvsala copilot needs your own Anthropic key (BYOK): GitHub-hosted models never go through a base URL, so there is nothing to meter. For Crush, Droid, Cline, Continue or Copilot in VS Code, bvsala doctor prints the exact configuration. Cursor (BYOK): it works through the OpenAI API base-URL override with your own key; its own models never reach a gateway on your machine. Gemini CLI: launch it with bvsala gemini.
installLicensePanel.pythonNote: Python? gateway.title: Claude Code on an API key? See its real spend, token by token.
gateway.body: One command puts a local meter in front of your terminal, with no changes to your code: export your service key and start your agent through bvsala. Your prompts don't pass through BiVelio's servers; they go to the provider you configure, and only counts and cost reach your dashboard.
gateway.note: The gateway measures, with your provider's own counter, every request whose usage the provider reports (for models in our price catalog) and starts with no keys at all (COMMUNITY mode): an optional service key adds the dashboard and org entitlements. On Anthropic models it also applies one lever by default, with no license or account: it moves cache writes from the one-hour TTL to the five-minute one only on turns where a large part of the prompt is new — such as a session's first turn or a compaction — and leaves chained turns as they are. That changes the price, never the content the model reads. It only has something to lower when your client pays per token and asks for the one-hour cache: Claude Code on an API key asks for the five-minute one unless you change it, and then the gateway only measures. The other levers stay off until you switch them on. The savings-mode skill is available for your caps, with its effect still to be measured. devs.title: Fewer bill headaches. Without changing provider.
devs.sub: Four facts about the package. None of them is a promise.

cards.title: Zero runtime dependencies
cards.body: A single ESM bundle. Nothing gets installed next to your code that we did not write; the exact tokenizer is an optional peer.

cards.title: One SavingsReport per call
cards.body: Four ledgers that are never summed, the cost with its basis (measured or estimated) and traces per stage. It is the same thing your dashboard reads.

cards.body: The SDK wraps the call inside your process. Your prompts never pass through BiVelio: we only ever receive counts and cost.

cards.title: Streaming, same report
cards.body: generateStream() hands you the answer as the provider writes it and closes with the same SavingsReport as generate(), under the same basis rules: the provider's final counter is read at the end of the stream, and a stream without it is reported as unmeasured and never counts as measured savings. With an output contract, the answer arrives validated, in one piece.

offers.title: Where do your tokens go: your app, or your coding agent?

gateway.what: One command puts a local meter in front of your terminal, with no code to change. It counts each request your provider reports usage for, with the provider's own counter — for models in our price catalog — and adds it up in your dashboard, by day and by model.
gateway.figureQue: estimated net reduction in list-price cost with the gateway's cache TTL change, after induced cache misses ({confianza} interval: {bajo} to {alto}). Counterfactual replay with a partially reconstructed baseline on {sesiones} Claude Code sessions from one organization; not a live A/B run or invoice reconciliation.
gateway.figureNote: Not a forecast for your team: it is one organization, one provider and list prices, and it is a small saving that shows where Anthropic spend is high. With a coding agent the gateway measures by default: this saving only applies when your client pays per token and asks for the one-hour cache, and Claude Code on an API key asks for the five-minute one unless you change it. On Anthropic models, with no license, it moves cache writes from the one-hour TTL to the five-minute one, only on turns where a large part of the prompt is new — such as a session's first turn or a compaction — and leaves the chained turns of a running session as they are. That changes the price, never what the model reads, and only what your provider's counter confirms counts in your savings report.

items.a: The open-source engine is free. Savings Cloud has a free plan, Measure, and two flat-fee plans billed per seat, Pro and Team. The fee is due whether or not you save, carries no commission on your savings, and does not include your LLM provider's usage: you keep paying that yourself, on their terms.

items.a: Community is the open-source engine on your infrastructure: no account, no BiVelio key and no telemetry by default. benchmarksPage.metaTitle: Public A/B bench: measure us | BiVelio Savings Layer
benchmarksPage.metaDescription: Four public batteries (GSM8K, BFCL, XSTest and MT-Bench), two arms metered by the provider's own usage counter, every figure with its n, its interval and its date. What it saves, what it doesn't, and the bugs the bench found.
benchmarksPage.title: Our A/B bench, in the open.
benchmarksPage.lede: We publish every run: four batteries on public datasets, {modelos} models, and both arms metered by the provider's own usage counter. Every figure carries its n, its interval and its date. What doesn't save is here too.

method.title: What is measured, and how
method.arms: Two arms, the same request. A goes straight to the provider, without the layer; B goes through the layer with its default configuration. Same prompt, same sampling, same output cap.
method.cost: Provider-reported usage and versioned list prices. Each arm is valued from the usage returned by the API and a dated list-price catalogue. Savings are 1 − cost(B) / cost(A) of the same run. Amounts are labelled measured, reference-valued or estimated according to their evidence; this is not invoice reconciliation.
method.intervals: {nivel} intervals. Each harness computes them (resampling whole question families, Wilson for refusal rates). An interval that crosses zero means “indistinguishable from zero”, and we say so.
method.package: The package you install. The A/B runs in the tables below were made on {version}: arm B runs the source of that tag, and its dist/index.js is byte-identical to the npm tarball's (sha256 {sha}). The weekly live bench is different: on every run it measures the source of main as it stands that day, before it is released.
method.guard: No shortcuts. Each harness watches the hosts it talks to and carries a per-model spend cap written in code. A model that could not be measured is reported as “not measured”, with the reason.
method.paper: <paper>Read the {paginas}-page research paper, {version} (PDF)</paper>: methods, evidence types and the limitations of each figure, revised after an external pre-publication review.

weekly.title: Weekly live bench
weekly.intro: Every week, and whenever we launch it by hand, one run takes every battery against every model: arm A straight to the provider, arm B through the layer built from the source of main at that moment. It is not a released version: it is what is about to be released. The run fails if any rule breaks, and a cell that could not be measured says why.
weekly.meta: Run of {fecha} · source of main at commit {commit} (package version {version}) · spent {gasto} of a {tope} cap · {medidas} of {celdas} cells measured.

reason.sin-clave: no key for this provider in the bench's environment
reason.cuota: the provider's quota or rate limit ran out, not the layer
reason.proveedor: no valid response from the provider in arm A
reason.tope-global: the run's overall spend cap was reached
reason.arnes-proveedor: this battery's harness only talks to Anthropic and OpenAI
reason.arnes-modelo: this battery's harness has no entry for this model
reason.arnes: error or timeout in the harness

weekly.note: “Layer failures” are errors in arm B that arm A did not have. “B − A” is the accuracy difference in GSM8K and BFCL, the refusal-rate difference in XSTest (McNemar's p, paired prompts) and, in MT-Bench, how often the judge prefers B (one half is a tie). “Report vs list-price cost” compares the layer's reported cost for arm B with the cost independently calculated from provider-reported usage at the same versioned list prices; it is not invoice reconciliation.
weekly.partialIntro: A partial run is launched by hand with only some models or batteries; for example, the other day's share of a model whose daily provider quota does not fit its four batteries in one day. It measures what it says, but it is not the weekly run: it does not count for publishing.

batteries.gsm8k: Math word problems with repeats and paraphrases: how much the cache saves and whether accuracy drops.
batteries.bfcl: Tool calls: the layer must not change a single one, and the whole catalog must arrive.
batteries.xstest: Refusals: the layer must not change when the model refuses, nor serve a refusal from cache.
batteries.mt-bench: Two-turn chat without repeats: the layer must not make cost, latency or quality worse.

savings.title: Measured savings per model
savings.intro: GSM8K, on a request stream where {rep} are exact repeats and {par} paraphrases. It is the battery with repeated traffic: your savings depend on how much yours repeats. Without repeats, see “What doesn't save”.
savings.originNote: Where the savings come from, position by position: “from the exact cache” is what A paid on the requests the layer served without calling the provider; “in the calls” is the difference on the ones that did reach it, mostly the provider's prefix cache (plus some output variation). Together they make the total.
savings.accuracyNote: Accuracy is measured on the questions with a published answer; the variants with a changed number only serve to check that the layer never hands back another question's answer.

gatewayTtl.title: The gateway's cache downgrade: a simulation, not an A/B
gatewayTtl.kind: This is a counterfactual replay with a partially reconstructed baseline, not one of this page's live A/B batteries. We took provider-reported usage from real Claude Code sessions at a single organization, our own, with one provider (Anthropic), and estimated costs at versioned list prices with and without the gateway's cache TTL change. It is not a live double-run or invoice reconciliation.
gatewayTtl.verdict: The verdict of the {fecha} report: the downgrade leaves a net {neto} of the bill ({netoUsd} out of {factura}), after subtracting the cache misses it causes itself.
gatewayTtl.thNet: Net, as a share of the bill
gatewayTtl.intervalsNote: Bootstrap with {remuestreos} resamples. Both intervals exclude zero: on this traffic, the downgrade makes money. The card on the home page quotes the per-session interval.
gatewayTtl.resultTitle: The result, with what it subtracts
gatewayTtl.resultNote: Percentages are shares of the list-price bill for the simulated requests ({factura}). The ceiling is the most any TTL policy could recover, even if it never missed. Each percentage is rounded separately.
gatewayTtl.thModelNet: Net, as a share of the model's bill
gatewayTtl.ugly: {modelo} is the ugly case: it accounts for {rebajas} of the downgrades and {fallos} of the misses, and its net is close to nothing. In the first period of the capture it actually lost: {perdida} of its bill. Its traffic is short threads that are rebuilt often and come back after the five minutes have passed. The rule really pays where session starts are expensive and rare.
gatewayTtl.howTitle: How it was done: the cache model, declared

how.rule: The rule is the one the gateway runs, not a copy: it moves cache writes from the one-hour TTL to the five-minute one when the new part is at least {umbral} of the request body.
how.baseline: The baseline is what the provider counted, with its real usage, where the downgrade was not yet active; where it already was, it is rebuilt by undoing it (see the limits). With the downgrade, the downgraded turn pays the five-minute write premium instead of the one-hour one.
how.miss: A caused miss: if the next turn of the same thread arrives after the five minutes and before the hour, what the downgraded turn wrote is no longer read from the cache, it is written again, and that cost is subtracted.
how.conservative: There is a conservative variant, which also treats the prefix shared between different threads as lost. It barely moves the figure: {neto}, with a few more misses ({fallos}).
how.aggregates: Aggregate figures only: no prompt, response, header or session identifier leaves the capture.

limits.oneOrg: One organization, one client, one provider. Claude Code against Anthropic, on our own traffic. No other coding agent and no other provider.
limits.listPrice: List price, simulated. It is not an invoice: it is the real usage, priced with the price catalog. Discounts, account tiers or a subscription would change the money.
limits.cacheModel: The cache model is a model. It assumes how the provider indexes its cache entries; it does not observe it. The conservative variant bounds that risk.
limits.rebuilt: Most of the baseline is reconstructed. {cuota} of the requests were recorded with the downgrade already active; there the baseline is rebuilt by undoing the real downgrade, and it is less firm than that of the first stretch. That first stretch, on its own, gives a much wider interval: {bajo} to {alto}.
limits.ceiling: The ceiling changes with the client. It depends on how many one-hour writes the coding agent sends, and recent versions of Claude Code send fewer: of the {peticiones} requests, {sinMarca} carried none to downgrade.
limits.gap: The gap between turns is measured from the arrival of each request, not from the end of the response: it counts a few misses too many, never too few.
limits.promise: It is not a forecast for your team. It is a small saving, from one traffic pattern, and other traffic can give another figure, including a worse one: look at the ugly case.

gatewayTtl.production: In production: since version {version} ({fecha}), the gateway subtracts the misses it observes, on the turn that suffers them, so the savings from this downgrade shown in your dashboard are net. What was recorded earlier is not recomputed, and the dashboard labels machines running an earlier gateway as “gross”.

tools.body: {alteradas} altered calls in {comparaciones} BFCL comparisons, {modelos} models, since {desde}. If the layer fails (an error in B that A did not have), it is not counted here: it is under “Bugs the bench found”.
tools.note: How it is counted: every comparison of every live run since that version, so a model measured twice (a pilot and the full run) adds both. That is why the figure can exceed the n of the tables, which show one run per model.

refusals.titleBroken: The refusal rate changed for {n} models
refusals.body: XSTest, {modelos} models measured: no A/B difference below p = {umbral} (McNemar, paired prompts). The layer delivered the text of {comprobados} responses unaltered ({alterados} altered).
refusals.caption: Refusal rate per model, without the layer (A) and with it (B), on the same prompts.
refusals.note: How it is counted: responses, not prompts. Every arm-B response is compared with the provider's text, repeats of the same prompt included, so there are more responses than prompts in the table.

noSavings.title: What doesn't save
noSavings.lead: Without repeats, savings are ≈ {cero}. We publish it anyway, because it is what you will see if your traffic does not repeat.
noSavings.why: MT-Bench is two-turn chat with a fresh layer per question: there is nothing for the cache to reuse, and the prompt almost never reaches the minimum the provider requires to cache a prefix. In BFCL every tool call is different. What these two batteries measure is that the layer makes nothing worse; the cost difference left over is noise in the model's output, not the layer.

bugs.notCountedWeekly: Not re-measured in a published report yet: the weekly bench of {fecha} (source of main with the fix, commit {commit}) measured {medidos} in this battery, but its summary counts only single-turn entries, not the multi-turn continuations where this failed. Until a report counts them, we do not count it as verified.

otra-pregunta.title: The uncalibrated semantic cache served another question's answer
otra-pregunta.body: With the semantic cache uncalibrated, a variant with another number (“three baskets” versus “two baskets”) could receive the original question's answer. Counted over the GSM8K variants.

herramientas-multiturno.title: The layer trimmed the tool catalog with no signal to do so
herramientas-multiturno.body: In multi-turn conversations, arm B sent fewer tools than arm A even though nothing indicated which ones were unneeded. Counted over the BFCL multi-turn conversations.

negativas-de-texto.title: Some refusals written as text were cached
negativas-de-texto.body: A refusal the model writes as text (without the API's signal) could be cached, repeated and credited as savings. Counted in XSTest prompts.

negativas-parciales.title: Partial refusals were cached and credited
negativas-parciales.body: A response that starts by complying and refuses further on (“If you mean harming someone, I can't help…”), or an apology followed by “I don't have access…”, was not recognized as a refusal: the layer could cache it, repeat it and credit it as savings. Counted in the weekly bench's XSTest prompts, with OpenAI and Claude models.

gemini-filtro-cacheado.title: A Gemini content filter was cached as an answer
gemini-filtro-cacheado.body: Gemini flags its filter with its own stop reason, which the layer did not recognize as a refusal, so it could cache and repeat it. Counted in XSTest prompts.

gemini-prompt-cache-key.title: Gemini did not go through the layer
gemini-prompt-cache-key.body: The layer sent a field specific to the OpenAI API to every compatible endpoint, and Gemini rejects it: every request in arm B failed. Counted in GSM8K requests.

gemini-thought-signature.title: With Gemini 3, the second turn with tools failed
gemini-thought-signature.body: The layer did not return the thought signature Gemini 3 requires on each tool call, so the next turn was rejected. Counted in BFCL multi-turn continuations.

gemini-nivel-de-pensamiento.title: With requests in parallel, Gemini's thinking-level correction reached the client as an error
gemini-nivel-de-pensamiento.body: Gemini Flash rejects the MINIMAL thinking level; the native adapter retries once with LOW and remembers the substitute. With two requests in flight through the same layer, one compared the rejection with the body the other had already corrected, did not recognize it and passed the error to the client. Counted as errors only with the layer, in the weekly bench's XSTest prompts with Gemini.

repro.title: How to reproduce it
repro.intro: The bench's code is in the open repository, and the method fits in five steps. With your own provider keys you can rerun it and compare figure by figure with our reports.

steps.dataset: The dataset. Download each public dataset at the commit in the table above and check every file's sha256 before using it. If it does not match, it is not the same dataset.
steps.package: The layer. Install @bivelio/savings-layer from npm at the version the report names and check the sha256 of dist/index.js: every report carries its own.
steps.arms: Two arms per prompt. A goes straight to the provider; B sends the same prompt, to the same model and with the same output cap, through the layer with its default configuration. Part of the prompts are repeated or paraphrased, as in real traffic, and the A/B order is randomised.
steps.cost: Usage and list prices document the valuation. Add each arm's cost from provider-reported usage at the versioned list price. Savings are 1 − cost B / cost A, with their interval; this is not invoice reconciliation.
steps.compare: Quality, in the same run. Score both arms' answers the same way (exact answer in GSM8K, tool call in BFCL, refusal or not in XSTest, a judge in MT-Bench) and compare them with the JSON report for the same battery and version.

repro.reportsIntro: Every run leaves a JSON report with its design, its limitations and every measured call: usage, cost per arm and how the answer was classified. They are served from this website.
repro.served: The reports are served as the bench wrote them, with one exception: data about the environment of whoever ran it (disk paths, email addresses) is removed. For XSTest no answer text is published, only its classification.

invite.title: Measure us yourself
invite.body: An independent measurement is worth more than ours. The bench's code is in the open repository: if you want to rerun the measurement, or measure the layer with your own harness or your own traffic, write to us and we will give you what you need to do it.
invite.subject: Independent measurement of the public bench

centre.classReplay: Counterfactual replay with a partially reconstructed baseline. It is not a live A/B, billed savings or an invoice reconciliation.
centre.compatible: Compatible does not mean measured: a model only counts here if it has a published run, and whatever could not be measured is stated with its reason.
centre.diagramA: Arm A: straight to the provider, without the layer
centre.diagramB: Arm B: through the layer, with its default configuration
centre.diagramMeter: The provider's usage meter measures both arms

ab.title: Both arms, model by model
ab.intro: GSM8K, the battery built to measure savings. Pick a measured model: A goes straight to the provider and B goes through the layer.
ab.hint: A is the reference; B goes through the layer.
ab.note: Only models with a measured run appear.
ab.forestTitle: Measured saving per model, with its interval
ab.forestHint: The dot is the estimate; the bar, the confidence interval; the line, zero. All on the same scale.

terms.interval: The estimate and, in brackets, its confidence interval. If the interval crosses zero, it cannot be told apart from zero.

howItWorks.metaTitle: Where does the saving install? · BiVelio Savings Layer
howItWorks.metaDescription: BiVelio Savings Layer runs in your infrastructure, as an SDK or local gateway. Open-source engine, optional Savings Cloud: what it saves, its limits, how it's measured.
howItWorks.title: Where does
howItWorks.lede: BiVelio Savings Layer is not an app, not an extension, not a ChatGPT setting. It's a piece of code a developer places inside their own application, right where that application calls your provider's API. It can only save where a per-token bill exists — and can only measure it where it sees every request go by.
howItWorks.s1Title: The layer lives inside your code
howItWorks.s1Sub: The same call, with and without the layer. Traffic always travels straight from your application to the provider — Savings Layer is not a middleman server and never sees your data from outside.
howItWorks.s1Note: That green box is an npm package inside the application's code. That's why the key question is never “what do I install?” but “who wrote the code that calls the API?” — that person is who can install it. The exceptions are a coding terminal like Claude Code and an app in any language that uses the official OpenAI or Anthropic SDK and lets you set its base URL: there the bvsala gateway sits in front without touching a line of code. That traffic is measured for models with a list price; the saving levers of the npm package do not run there, and the gateway's own apply only to Anthropic traffic, free and with no key.
howItWorks.s2Sub: Four ways of using AI, and what Savings Layer can do in each one.
howItWorks.caseChatSub: app or web, free or paid
howItWorks.caseChatBody: You pay a flat fee (or nothing): there is no per-token bill to reduce, and it's a closed product where nobody can place software between the app and its models. Savings Layer's saving simply doesn't apply here — and no product can honestly promise it there.
howItWorks.caseClaudeBody: Flat subscription: no token invoice to meter — but there are caps (the five-hour window and the weekly one). That is exactly what the savings-mode skill is for: free, uploaded to claude.ai in a minute, attacking the two masses that burn cap. Its effect will be published once measured — never before.
howItWorks.caseCodeBody: On a subscription the fee is flat — but capped: the same skill installs with a single command and stretches the same weekly cap. With an API key there is a real token invoice — and the meter is already running: with no BiVelio key at all, “bvsala claude” launches Claude Code through the local gateway, without touching a line of code. The gateway meters what passes through it on your machine, with the usage your provider reports, and on exit tells you how many requests it metered, which ones it could not, and why. On Anthropic models it also moves cache writes from the one-hour TTL to the five-minute one only on turns where a large part of the prompt is new (a session's first turn, a compaction): a saving computed on your provider's own token count, never on an estimate. That needs Claude Code to ask for the one-hour cache, and on an API key it does not unless you set it: by default the gateway only measures. With a Savings Cloud key you see your spend in the dashboard as well, token by token.
howItWorks.caseAppBody: The case Savings Layer exists for. Your app calls the API with your key, the provider bills every token, and the layer installs in two steps: package and wrapping the call. From the first request it returns a SavingsReport with the saving, split into measured and estimated.
howItWorks.s3Sub: The product has two different numbers, and they shouldn't be mixed.
howItWorks.mBeforeBody: The free cloud plan runs the layer in shadow mode on your own traffic and shows what it would have saved, request by request. It changes nothing and applies nothing — that's why it carries the “estimate” tag. No plan at all? Open core: the local levers run with no key and zero telemetry.
howItWorks.mAfterBody: Every call returns a SavingsReport: the calls you never paid for and the net saving per request. Auditable, request by request, on your own infrastructure.
howItWorks.s4Title: The full install, if you build an app
howItWorks.snip3: wrap the call — this is the entire code change
howItWorks.billDepends: on how much your traffic repeats

sdk.body: An npm package that wraps the provider call in your own code. It runs in the same process as your application: there is no server in between.
sdk.p1: For whoever develops the application that calls the API, on Node.js.

gateway.body: bvsala starts a proxy on your own machine. You point the base URL of the official OpenAI or Anthropic SDK at it, or launch Claude Code through it, without touching your code.

seat.title: How a seat is counted and billed
seat.cycle: The seat fee is billed through Stripe for each monthly or yearly cycle of your subscription, counted from the day it starts.
seat.paidAlways: The seat fee is paid whether or not the Software produces any saving.
seat.vat: Amounts exclude VAT. Checkout asks for your billing address and, optionally, your VAT number; both are printed on your invoice.
seat.what: A seat is one machine or service identity that runs the Software, not a person. You choose how many seats your subscription covers (up to {max} at checkout), and your license covers that many.
seat.counted: Each calendar month (UTC), BiVelio counts as in use every distinct seat identifier that was active on at least {dias} different days of that month. Identities flagged as CI or ephemeral runners are not counted. Your dashboard compares that count with the seats your subscription covers.
seat.overage: If in a month you use more seats than your subscription covers, the difference is billed once, when the month closes: what those extra seats cost for one month on your plan. On monthly billing it is added to your next invoice and your subscribed quantity goes up to the seats in use. On annual billing it is invoiced at month close, at the annual rate divided by twelve, and your subscribed quantity does not change. If the count isn't reliable — for example, because you rotated a service-account key that month — it is not charged: we review it by hand.
seat.identifier: How a seat identifier is formed, and everything else the Software sends to BiVelio, is on the <privacy>privacy page</privacy>.
seat.provider: The fee does not include your LLM provider's usage: you keep your provider and pay for its use on their terms.
seat.manage: You choose and pay for a plan from <account>your account</account>, in the dashboard, through Stripe's hosted checkout. Changes to an existing subscription are made in Stripe's billing portal, which opens from that same page. This page does not charge anything.

commission.title: Earlier plan with a commission (closed to new customers)
commission.optional: This plan is no longer offered to new customers. If your subscription is already on it, you keep it unchanged, and the terms below still govern it: a lower seat fee plus a commission only on savings you can reconcile with your provider's invoice. Pro and Team never carry it; their statement shows the commission that would have applied only as a reference.
commission.seat: Seat fee under this arrangement: {monthly} per seat per month, or {yearly} per seat per year, in {currency}.
commission.only: A commission is charged only on measured savings: savings labelled {labels} in your usage records. Savings labelled {never} never carry commission.
commission.measured: A measured saving is established from your LLM provider's own usage counter for that request.
commission.reference: A reference saving, for a repeated request the Software served without calling your provider, is established from your provider's counter for the identical earlier request that did run, under the rule shown on your statement ({regla}).
commission.valued: Both are valued at the per-token prices the Software applied to that request: those of a cost model you configure, where you configure one, and otherwise your provider's list prices in the price catalogue included in the Software.
commission.flatRate: Traffic the Software identifies as a flat-rate provider subscription (a Claude or ChatGPT subscription used through the local gateway) is metered but credited no measured saving, so it carries no commission.
commission.elision: The value of input tokens your provider reports as cleared from context is recorded, but it is not part of the commission base.
commission.tiersIntro: The period's measured savings are converted to {currency} and split into marginal tiers, each charged at its own rate:
commission.ceiling: No tier's rate exceeds {max}, so before the commission is rounded to the cent you keep at least {garantia} of the period's measured savings. The seat fee is separate.
commission.fx: Measured savings are counted in US dollars and converted at the European Central Bank reference rate fetched when the period is closed; your statement shows the rate used.
commission.rounding: The commission is rounded to the nearest cent. A commission below {minimo} is not invoiced and is not carried over to another period.
commission.zero: A period with no measured savings carries no commission.

calibration.title: Calibration period
calibration.body: The first calendar month (UTC) in which your organization reports any usage is a calibration period, however little of that month remains. It carries no commission, and its statement still shows the commission that would have applied.

exemption.title: Exemption from the commission
exemption.body: No commission is charged for a period that BiVelio closes while your account is exempt from it. An account is exempt when BiVelio grants it an exemption and, until a payment is made on the account, when its subscription was activated with a promotional code that waives the seat fee in full for its entire term. The statement still shows the commission that would have applied.

statement.title: Statement and invoice
statement.body: The commission is calculated per calendar month (UTC). After a month ends, BiVelio closes it: your dashboard's statement for that month is sealed with the measured base, the tiers, the exchange rate and the price-catalogue version, and the commission is invoiced from that statement through Stripe, on an invoice separate from the seat fee.

privacyPage.metaDescription: The exact list of what the SDK and the local gateway send to BiVelio, what they never send, and how long BiVelio keeps it.
privacyPage.title: What leaves your infrastructure
privacyPage.governs: This page describes how the service works today; the <license>LICENSE</license> and the <terms>BiVelio Terms</terms> govern.
privacyPage.lede: What the Software (the SDK and the local gateway) sends to BiVelio, what it never sends, and how long BiVelio keeps it.

never.title: Never sent to BiVelio
never.content: The content of your requests and responses: prompts, system instructions, messages, tool definitions, tool arguments and results, retrieved documents, and completions.
never.credentials: The credentials you use with your LLM provider: API keys, OAuth tokens, or other authorization headers.
never.path: That content and those credentials travel only between your systems and the LLM provider you configure.

usage.title: Usage records
usage.when: The SDK sends usage records only when you configure a license server or metering URL; the local gateway always does. Each batch carries your BiVelio service-account key, which identifies your organization, and the Software's surface and version in the {header} header.
usage.limit: Each record is limited to the fields below. BiVelio's ingest rejects any record that carries a field not on this list.

ids.title: Identifiers
ids.body: A request identifier generated on your side (at random, or by your own generator). For a repeated request valued by reference, the identifier and time of the earlier request whose provider counter is used. A seat identifier: a value you set, or an opaque value computed on your machine as a keyed hash (HMAC), keyed with your service-account key, of the platform, CPU architecture, runtime executable path, host name, operating-system user name and home directory; those underlying values are never sent. Through the local gateway, the session and sub-agent identifiers your coding agent attaches to its own requests (for example, Claude Code's session id), only when they are plain identifiers. An organization hint (BiVelio always derives your organization from the key). A flag marking CI or ephemeral runners.

model.title: Model and time
model.body: The identifier of the model that served the request: the model named in the request or, where the Software sent the request to another model under a setting you enabled, that model; for a self-hosted or Azure deployment, the name you gave it. And the time of the request.

counts.title: Counts
counts.body: LLM calls executed and avoided; input and output tokens before and after the Software's optimizations, including tokens removed, compressed, or read from the provider's cache; and the cache outcome.

cost.title: Cost
cost.body: Cost figures computed by the Software from its price catalogue, or from a cost model you supply: baseline cost, actual cost, the net-saving ratio, the basis of the figures (measured, reference, estimated, shadow or unmeasured), and the value, at the provider's cache-read price, of input tokens your provider reported as cleared from context. Shown apart and never used to calculate the fees: the discount your provider's own prompt cache gave the request and the cache-write premium it billed.

verification.title: Optional verification (SDK only, off by default)
verification.when: If you turn on the SDK's verification option, the SDK sends a sample of the requests it served to your own provider again, without optimization, and discards that second response. For each sampled request it sends BiVelio, through a separate channel, only the fields below; that channel also rejects any other field, and nothing it receives is used for billing.

sample.title: Each sampled request
sample.body: The label verification, the request identifier and time; the model requested and the model that served; the cache outcome; the category of the request and the outcome of the check; the input, cached-input and output tokens and the cost of the served request and of the unoptimized copy; how the copy finished and whether it met the response contract; and the per-token prices applied.

counts.title: Daily counts
counts.body: For each day, the number of requests in each category, including the requests excluded from the check.

batch.title: Each batch
batch.body: A random batch identifier, used to discard duplicates, and the two lists above.

other.title: Other requests to BiVelio
other.body: The Software also fetches its current license token and the signed license revocation list, and the local gateway fetches your organization's feature entitlements. These requests carry your service-account key where authentication is required, and no request data.
other.network: Like any HTTPS request, all of the above also reveals ordinary network metadata, such as your IP address.

retention.title: What BiVelio keeps, and for how long
retention.intro: The ingest adds each usage record to daily totals: per day, per model, per seat and per gateway session. Individual rows are kept only in the places below, and a daily job deletes each row once it is older than its period:

items.seen: Request identifiers, kept to discard duplicate records: {dias} days.
items.reference: Repeated requests valued by reference (request identifiers, model, time and the provider counter used), the rows behind your statement's download: {dias} days.
items.verificationSamples: Verification samples and their daily counts: {dias} days.

retention.noSchedule: Daily totals, seat activity and your sealed statements have no automatic deletion schedule today.

use.title: What BiVelio uses it for
use.body: To operate licensing and revocation, show your dashboard, count seats in use, and calculate the fees described on the <pricing>pricing page</pricing>.

account.title: Your account on this website
account.body: Your sign-in e-mail, your organization and your billing details (payments are processed by Stripe) are covered by <policy>BiVelio's privacy policy</policy>.
